title: Greening the city
location: Myers Park Cottage, 72 Greys Avenue, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Here at Myers Park Cottage we are lucky enough to be hosting Greening the City - a free programme supporting Auckland city centre residents, businesses and workers to share the resources, knowledge and community to grow their own plants from seed.
We have close to $10,000 of resources to give away:

compost
seed raising mix
professional propagation trays
plus a huge array of seeds.

Every participant then gets 10 weeks of tailored email support - how-to videos, troubleshooting, the lot. 
On our open days, professional urban farmers will run drop-in, family-friendly workshops where people can learn how to sow seeds and take home their own resource pack.
In August we will regroup at Myers Park Cottage to share our collectively grown seedlings and plant out a beautiful community garden full of flowers, fruit trees and vegetables.
So bring your gardening gloves and together we can do some planting around the cottage and we can start spreading some seeds to help feed others.
In partnership with Auckland Council and Levi Brinsdon-Hall from Delicious Revolution.

title: Music Repair Café
location: Grey Lynn Community Centre, 510 Richmond Road, Grey Lynn, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Repair Café Aotearoa NZ and Holding Space Aotearoa have banded together to bring you our 3rd ‘Music Repair Cafe’, Tune-Up for Your Instruments - this time in Grey Lynn for NZ Music Month in May!
Our goal is to empower you to care for your instruments, provide practical assistance where possible and foster a culture of repair and sustainability within our music community.
Connect with fellow music lovers, share your experiences, and learn from our knowledgeable volunteers in a friendly and supportive environment.
Plus enjoy live music from Songwriters 4 Climate Action and more!
What we offer:
Our team of skilled volunteers will be on hand to provide a range of free services, including on the spot minor repairs.
We'll tackle small repairs and adjustments right at the event, if possible. This could include things like:

restring instruments (you supply your favourite strings or can purchase some if available)
cable testing
cable repair if possible
solder loose connections
woodwind and brass instrument check ups
orchestral string instrument check ups
repairing guitar straps, instrument bags, costume etc.

We also offer advice on:

recycling wires
recycling batteries
recycling strings
instrument cleaning and maintenance.

If we can’t fix it, we offer instrument assessment: Bring your instrument in (in a case if possible), and our experienced repairers will give it a thorough check-up. We'll diagnose the problem and offer advice on what needs to be done to get it working again.
Important information:
While our volunteers will do their best to assist you with your instrument repairs, please understand that we cannot guarantee that all items can be fully repaired during the event. The complexity of some repairs may require more time, parts, specialised tools or professional attention.
Please note this particular repair cafe caters just to musical gear. Check out another repair cafe for fixing other appliances, clothes etc.
This community event is supported by Waitematā

title: From Vibe Coding to Production with the AI Driven Software Life Cycle

description:

We're excited to invite you to the May Auckland AWS Tools and Programming meetup!

This month, we are focusing heavily on the intersection of AI and software engineering. We are thrilled to host two fantastic speakers: [Iain Phillips](https://www.linkedin.com/in/phillipsiain/) (VP of Engineering @ Pushpay) and [Cecilia Yin ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cecilia-yin)(Solutions Architect @ AWS).

Join Iain for a frank talk on what it takes to transform an AI-generated demo into a reliable, scalable, and secure enterprise product. Learn how to embrace product contributions from non-engineering roles without compromising on quality, compliance, or security. Get ahead of the curve and discover whose job it really is to harden AI code before your guardrails completely disappear.

**Part 2: Cecilia Yin \| Solutions Architect @ AWS**

Whether you are an engineer, an architect, or just curious about the future of tech, come find out how AWS is helping teams navigate this massive shift. Get ahead of the curve and learn how to reinvent your engineering workflow before the old methods leave you behind.

title: Beyond the Hype: Level up your AI game as a Tester
location: 37 Galway Street, Auckland
description:
We've been here before. Manual testing gave way to automation, and the Testers who adapted thrived. AI is that moment again, and it's moving faster.
If you've ever thought "there's so much going on with AI right now, I don't know where to start" or "I'm using it a bit but what's actually next?", this session is built for you.

This is for Testers/ QA/ QE engineers and Leads at every stage of the journey, whether you just got sign-off to try an AI tool or you're already using one to write your e2e tests. We'll make the case for why QE judgment matters more than ever in a world of non-deterministic software, and walk through a practical five-level framework for getting AI working in your day-to-day.
Then we roll up our sleeves.

**Format**
A short talk talk followed by a hands-on workshop where we'll brainstorm real use cases together. The workshop is structured so you can contribute at whatever level you're at. If you've never used an AI tool for testing, you'll leave with your first concrete use case. If you're already automating with AI, we'll push into the harder problems.

**What you'll take away**
A clear next step to "where do I actually start?" You'll leave with a working mental model for what good AI-assisted testing looks like at each stage of maturity, and at least one thing you can try the next day.

**Agenda**
5:00 PM – Doors open
Drinks, nibbles & networking (thanks to Aurorl)
5:30 PM – Talk
6:00 PM – Open Q&A
6:15 PM – Workshop
7:00 PM onwards – More networking

**About Francis Ho**
[Francis ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/francis-ho/)is the Director of Engineering at Auror, a New Zealand-born platform helping retailers prevent crime and make stores safer for the people who work and shop in them.

He started his career as a developer, switched to testing because he found it more fun, and has spent the years since working across healthcare, fintech, big data, and retail crime intelligence.

title: The highs and lows of building Agentically
location: Level 5, 22 Viaduct Harbour Avenue, Auckland
description:
*Serko recently launched the closed beta of Serko.ai - an autonomous, multi-agent AI solution set to redefine business travel. CTO Simon Young will discuss the highs and lows of building agentically, within the SDLC and within the product, and share some hot takes on the state of AI within software engineering.*

Simon is a highly respected New Zealand technology executive and currently serves as Chief Technology Officer at Serko. He brings more than 20 years of experience leading engineering, product, and technology teams in high-growth software businesses.
Simon joined Serko in 2023 as Vice President of Engineering and was appointed CTO in 2024. In this role, he is responsible for driving Serko’s global technology strategy, fostering innovation, and scaling the company’s engineering capability as it expands internationally.
Prior to Serko, Simon held senior executive positions including Chief Product and Technology Officer at Trade Me and Vice President of Engineering at Halter. He is widely regarded as a strong engineering and product leader with deep expertise in SaaS platforms, large-scale software development, and building high-performing technology teams.
Simon is known for combining strategic vision with strong technical leadership, making him one of New Zealand’s most accomplished CTOs in the software and technology sector.

title: Last Laughs Awards Gala
location: SkyCity Theatre, Corner Hobson Street and, Wellesley Street West, Auckland City Centre, Auckland
description:
The Festival finale. The awards night. A stacked live show - all in one.
Hosted by the beloved Guy Montgomery (Fred Award winner, Logie winner, and the mastermind behind Guy Montgomery's Guy Mont-Spelling Bee), Last Laughs is the Festival’s final night out – where the stakes are high, the room is buzzing, and the big moments happen in real time.
It’s also your last chance to see this year’s nominees do their thing in the same room, one after the other: the five Billy T nominees hit the stage for their final Festival sets, then we meet the three Fred Award finalists (revealed only around 48 hours beforehand) and see why their shows have risen to the top. While the judges deliberate, a secret headliner takes over, before we present the Billy T Award and The Fred Award live on the night.
The Billy T Award winner takes home the iconic yellow towel plus a cash prize, and the Fred Award winner scores the legendary gumboot trophy (and a cash prize too) – and this year The Fred turns 20!
Last Laughs: Awards Gala is a night for audiences too. This is your chance to rub shoulders with your favourite comedians, catch the live reactions, and be in on all the laughs.
If you want one night that feels like the whole Festival in one room, this is it.
